issues.detail: Rule condition uses prev_in & ~in (any falling bit) but example expects full 0xFFFFFFFF capture from all-ones to all-zeros; condition would also capture on partial falls, which example does not distinguish but is consistent only for full fall. No contradiction per se, but condition is broader than example; example does not test partial fall.
issues.spec_evidence: capture when the input signal changes from 1 in one clock cycle to 0 the next

issues.detail: Spec says capture per bit when that bit falls; contract condition (prev_in & ~in) != 0 triggers capture of all falling bits simultaneously, which matches per-bit semantics, but alternative semantics could be 'capture only if any bit falls and then set all bits' vs 'set only falling bits'. Contract sets only falling bits via out |= prev_in & ~in implied by example? Example full fall cannot distinguish.
issues.spec_evidence: For each bit in a 32-bit vector, capture when the input signal changes from 1 in one clock cycle to 0 the next.
issues.alternative: On any falling edge of any bit, set all 32 output bits to 1 (global sticky) rather than per-bit sticky.

issues.detail: R3_hold example uses in=1 then in=3 (bit0 stays 1, bit1 rises) and expects out=0 throughout; consistent with no falling bits. However R3 condition (prev_in & ~in)==0 includes cases where bits rise; hold is correct. No contradiction, but example does not exercise hold after a capture.
issues.spec_evidence: the output will remain 1 until the register is reset

issues.detail: R1 example vectors show reset=1 with in=0xFFFFFFFF then reset=1 with in=0 then reset=0 with in=0, expected out=0 each cycle. With sync reset, out=0 on reset cycles is correct; after deassert with in=0 and prev_in=0, no fall, out stays 0. Consistent.

Contract states update_during_reset true and reset first_released_cycle 'cycle after reset deasserts at posedge'; spec only says active high synchronous reset, which implies reset sampled at posedge and out cleared same cycle. No verbatim evidence for 'first_released_cycle' phrasing but semantics consistent.

Derived outputs for R2 example: cycle1 reset=0 in=0xFFFFFFFF prev_in unknown/0 -> out=0; cycle2 in=0 prev=0xFFFFFFFF -> out=0xFFFFFFFF; cycle3 in=0 prev=0 -> hold 0xFFFFFFFF; cycle4 hold. Matches expected.
